headline: Bitcoin ended Friday near $68,000 after falling below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months, as higher bond yields and the Nvidia shake-up weighed on tech and Strategy faces removal from MSCI indexes.

market.asOf: Read about 23:57 UTC Fri 13 Nov (06:57 Sat 14 Nov Bangkok): BTC and SOL from CoinGecko, ETH from CoinMarketCap. CoinMarketCap showed BTC at $69,293 (-5.97%) at the same time. Use the live prices on this page.

stories.title: Bitcoin ends the week near $68,000 as yields and Nvidia turmoil hit risk assets
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday for the first time in nearly three months, per Yahoo Finance, and slipped under its 200-week moving average, per CoinDesk. Rising Treasury yields and hotter-than-hoped inflation have markets expecting a Fed rate hike in December, and chip stocks fell again as investors digested Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO. Higher rates make risky assets like crypto less attractive.
points: Friday's low differs by source: $67,652 in CoinDesk's 4:17am ET update, $67,922 per CryptoTicker (CoinGecko data).
At 5:55pm ET Friday bitcoin was $68,369 (-4.21%), ether $1,930 (-4.34%) and solana $78.24 (-4.18%), per Business Upturn.
More than $1.3B of leveraged bets were forcibly closed in 24 hours, about $677M of them on bitcoin, per CoinGlass via CryptoTicker.
At the close the Nasdaq fell 0.9% and the S&P 500 0.4%, while the Dow rose 0.1%; the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17%, per Yahoo Finance.
After October's wholesale prices (PPI) rose 0.3% on the month and 6.5% on the year, CME FedWatch showed 89.7% odds of a quarter-point December hike and 10.3% for a half-point, per InvestmentNews.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving bitcoin funds; Strategy to be dropped from MSCI indexes
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the main way many Americans hold bitcoin through a brokerage, have had a run of daily outflows. Separately, MSCI will remove Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, from its indexes at the end of November, which could force index funds to sell its shares. CoinDesk also quotes Xapo Bank's CEO saying investors may be selling bitcoin to fund the Anthropic IPO.
points: Bitcoin ETFs had $284M of net outflows on 12 November, the sixth day in a row, with $204M from BlackRock's IBIT, per SoSoValue data reported by KuCoin News.
MSCI removes Strategy after the close on 30 November, per CoinDesk.

Estimates of the forced selling differ: about $1.6B per CoinDesk (citing BloFin and Strategy's analysis); about $2.8B per Strategy's estimate as reported by Yahoo Finance, which cites J.P. Morgan at up to $8.8B if other index providers follow.
Strategy shares were down 3.64% at $110.24 at 10:05am ET Friday, per Yahoo Finance.
Anthropic's IPO could raise up to $64.4B, per CoinDesk, which quotes Xapo Bank's CEO saying investors may be selling bitcoin and other liquid assets to fund allocations.

stories.title: US government sues Arkansas to protect prediction markets like Kalshi
stories.summary: The US government and the CFTC sued Arkansas, arguing federal law overrides the state's gambling law for federally regulated prediction-market exchanges. Prediction markets let people trade on outcomes like elections or sports through regulated apps, and the fight decides whether states can ban them. There is no ruling yet.
points: The suit was filed on 12 November in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas, per InvestmentNews.
Arkansas filed its own action against Kalshi on 4 November; its law allows penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, per InvestmentNews.
The federal government has similar actions against 10 other states, and early injunctions have favored it in Arizona, Illinois and Minnesota, per InvestmentNews.
Robinhood's prediction-market contracts rose 136% from a year earlier in October, per its monthly operating data.

briefs.title: US moves to seize $1.2B from North Korea's Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department has court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack and disrupted a deepfake scam it calls FaceStealer, per The Block.

briefs.title: Nvidia falls again after Huang's exit
briefs.summary: HSBC downgraded Nvidia to hold, Apple passed it as the most valuable company and AMD fell 8.8% on Friday, per Forbes. Nvidia reports results on Tuesday.
